newsitem.title: USA: U.S. airlines raise leisure fares three percent.
newsitem.headline: U.S. airlines raise leisure fares three percent.

text.p: U.S. airlines quietly raised leisure fares three percent, but left business fares untouched.
Carriers such as Continental Airlines Inc, US Airways Group Inc and Trans World Airlines Inc said they raised fares by three percent in most markets.
The fare increases went into effect on Friday and throughout the weekend, the airlines said.
"We matched our competitors and went along with that fare increase," TWA spokesman John McDonald said.

TWA said its fare increase was in effect throughout the United States, but excluded markets that are served by its competitor Southwest Airlines Co. Southwest enacted fare increases that varied market to market, which TWA matched, McDonald said.
Southwest could not be immediately reached for comment.
UAL Corp, parent of United Airlines, and Northwest Airlines Inc did not comment immediately on whether or not they had raised fares.
"We think the airlines are clearly testing the pricing limits of what the market can bear," said Lehman Brothers analyst Brian Harris in a research report.
"The fact that business-type fares were not raised suggest that these fares are already encountering significant price resistance," Harris said.
